why: no model has been rendered and compared with the unit
claim: A modulation wave byte indexes five fixed shapes and computes nothing, and four of the five are the shapes the page names them. Read on two types that drive different quantities with the same byte -- one swinging its output's level by more than the whole of its own mean, the other swinging the balance between its channels by forty decibels -- the entry printed `Tri` returns a triangle, `Sqr` a square and `Saw1` and `Saw2` a sawtooth, each nearer the shape it is named after than any other by both of the two readings taken, on both types, 8 readings out of 8. `Saw1` and `Saw2` are one shape run two ways: no reading of magnitudes can separate them, which the two candidates sitting exactly zero apart under both scores says outright, and what separates them is that one spends nine tenths of its cycle climbing and the other one tenth. The fifth entry is not what it is printed. `Sin` carries a third harmonic of four to six hundredths where a sine has none and a triangle has a ninth, and a fifth harmonic of two thousandths where a triangle has a twenty-fifth -- so it is neither, and it is a sine made cheaply. Which cheap sine is not settled and is queued. The shape is a shape of a multiplier and not of a level: the same cycles come back clean read in amplitude and warped read in decibels, which is what a gain swung linearly does to a logarithm and not what a gain swung in decibels would do to either. Three readings stood against this and each had a run; all three ran. The five shapes are not these two types': the third place the same five names are printed returns the same five, entry for entry, no further apart than 0.0122 in any harmonic either reading carries, with both sawtooths climbing the same way round. The depth byte scales the cycle rather than reshaping it, and what looked like a shape moving with depth was the reading's own logarithm: read as a difference between two channels in decibels the third harmonic sits a median 0.0582 from the linear reading at the top of the byte and 0.0166 at a quarter of it, converging on it as the swing shrinks and the logarithm straightens. And the entry printed `Sin` is not the parabola. It is not the parabola, and it is refused from both sides at once. Rendered onto one of this unit's own takes and read back through the whole stage, the parabola returns a third harmonic of 0.0409 where the unit returns 0.0600, and a fifth of 0.0054 where the unit returns 0.0029 -- too little of the one and more than twice too much of the other, which no scaling of a candidate can fix in both directions at once. What fits is a sine carrying a small third harmonic and almost nothing above it: a sine carrying a fifteenth of its third lands 0.0038 away where the parabola lands 0.0112, 3.0 times as far. That is a description of the cycle and not a name for what makes it, and this file does not give it one.
named: a table of five fixed modulator shapes, indexed by a byte, multiplying
adds: Each record says what one cycle of one setting's modulator looks like, as a curve and as harmonics, and puts no name on it. What is read out of them here is which of five named shapes each cycle is -- which is a comparison against a page and against four analytic shapes, neither of which is in either record -- and that the five are one table because two types driving different quantities return them.
refutedBy: A sixth setting of the byte returning a sixth shape, which would make this a range rather than a table of five. Or any of the four named entries coming back as something else on a third type, by more than the two types here differ from each other. Or the harmonics moving with the depth byte, which would mean the cycles reported are one point of a surface and the table is not a table of shapes at all.
whatItWouldChange: A modulator is five entries and an accumulator. There is nothing to fit, nothing to tune, and no per-type constant: two types driving different quantities return the same five cycles from the same byte.
`Saw1` and `Saw2` are one shape and its mirror, not two. A renderer that made them two ramps with different slopes would be wrong about both.

The modulator multiplies. A renderer that swung a level in decibels would put a second harmonic into every one of the five, which is what the decibel reading of these very takes shows and the amplitude reading does not.

eraPriors.claim: A modulator on a fixed-point part of this period is a phase accumulator and a shape read off it. A triangle, a square and a sawtooth are each one or two operations on the accumulator itself and cost nothing; a sine is the only one of the five that has to be stored or approximated, and it is the only one that came back as something other than its name.
eraPriors.why: It says why four of five would be exact and the fifth would not, which is the shape of what was found rather than something read into it. It carries none of the claim: every entry was measured.
eraPriors.wouldBeWrongIf: The triangle or the sawtooth had come back inexact too, which would point at the reading rather than at the part. They did not: the sawtooth's harmonics fall as one over the order to within a few hundredths and the square's to within a twentieth.

alternatives.reading: The entry printed `Sin` is a sine after all, and the third harmonic is something the reading put there.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: The entry beside it on the same takes. `Tri` returns two to four times this one's third harmonic through the same frames, the same fold and the same detrend, so the method does not hand every entry the same amount -- and a reading that added a fortieth of a third harmonic to everything would have moved the sawtooth's away from one over the order, which it did not.

alternatives.reading: The entry printed `Sin` is the parabola a part of this period reaches for when it has no room for a table: one multiply-and-subtract on the phase.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: Both of its harmonics, in opposite directions. Rendered onto one of this unit's own takes and read back through the whole stage it returns 0.0409 at the third harmonic where the unit returns 0.0600, and 0.0054 at the fifth where the unit returns 0.0029. Too little of one and more than twice too much of the other is not a candidate that needs scaling; the two errors cannot be reduced together. The two types carrying this entry agree with each other to 0.0027 at the third harmonic and 0.0027 at the fifth, so the gap is many times what the reading fails to repeat.

separatedBy.observable: The fifth and seventh harmonics of that entry's cycle, read off a longer take at a slower rate so more cycles fold into one. The third already agrees; a parabola puts 0.008 in the fifth and 0.003 in the seventh, and a parabola with its own square added back puts under a thousandth in either.

predicts.a stored table: Whatever the table holds, which is not predicted -- but a table fine enough to be called a sine puts nothing measurable in either.

separatedBy.divergence: 0.007 in the fifth harmonic, which is the gap between the two candidates that are not a table.
separatedBy.sensitivity_here: 0.002, what this run's fifth harmonic came back at on a cycle folded from eighteen. Four times as many cycles is half of that, which is where the margin below comes from.

run.stimulus: the same held note with the rate byte at the slowest setting the take can still carry three cycles of, and the take lengthened

alternatives.reading: The five shapes are these two types', and the one other place the same five names are printed reaches a table of its own.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: The third place read. Entry for entry the five shapes land no further apart than 0.0122 in any harmonic either reading carries, and both sawtooths climb the same way round -- on a type reached at a different parameter number with four stages in front of it.

separatedBy.observable: The same sweep on `04 06 / 40 03 12`, which is the only other place this unit prints these five names -- a tremolo and pan stage inside a multi-effect rather than a type of its own, reached at a different parameter number, with four stages in front of it.

predicts.one table: The same five cycles, to the harmonics already reported.
predicts.a table per type: At least one entry whose harmonics are not these, by more than the two types here differ from each other.

separatedBy.divergence: 0.12, how far a triangle sits from a square under the harmonic reading, taken as what a different table would have to be worth.
separatedBy.sensitivity_here: 0.02, how far the two types already read differ from each other on the entry they differ most on.

run.stimulus: the same held note with this type's compressor, overdrive, equaliser and phaser stages switched out or held flat

alternatives.reading: The depth byte beside this one scales the cycle, so the shape is the same shape at every depth.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: Upheld rather than refuted, and recorded as what it turned out to be. Read at three settings of the depth byte the cycle is the same cycle; the decibel reading's own warp accounts for the whole of the apparent change, sitting 0.0582 from the unwarped reading at the top of the byte and 0.0166 at a quarter of it.

separatedBy.observable: The same five entries at a depth well below full. Every cycle was read at 127 here, so nothing in this file says what the shape is anywhere else on that byte.

predicts.a depth that scales: The same harmonics at every depth, since a harmonic is reported relative to the first.
predicts.a depth that reshapes: Harmonics that move with it -- which is what a depth applied by clipping the modulator rather than by scaling it would do.

separatedBy.divergence: 0.11, a triangle's own third harmonic, taken as what a reshaping worth the name would be.
separatedBy.sensitivity_here: 0.02, how far the two types here differ on one entry's harmonics.

run.stimulus: the same held note with the depth byte at 32 and at 96

alternatives.reading: The small third harmonic is the unit's, but what puts it there is a short sine table read coarsely rather than a sine deliberately softened.

separatedBy.observable: Where the energy sits above the seventh harmonic. A table of N points joined by straight lines puts its error at harmonics near N and its multiples, not at the third; a softened sine puts a third harmonic and nothing else. The reading cannot go there: the amplitude track is taken on a twenty millisecond frame, so at the slowest rate this modulator runs the eighth harmonic is already at the frame's own corner.

predicts.a softened sine: a third harmonic and nothing above the seventh
predicts.a short table: a third harmonic and a rise again near the table's length

separatedBy.sensitivity_here: 0.0027, what the two types carrying this entry fail to agree on.
separatedBy.why_not_separable: Not by this stage on this unit. A modulator running at a few hertz has its eighth harmonic in the tens of hertz, and the envelope is read on a frame chosen to hold the lowest note the run uses. Reading higher would need the modulation applied to something whose envelope can be tracked faster, which is a different stimulus rather than a different setting.
